full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Delwar Hossain, J:- This Rule was issued upon an application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceedings of Special case No.2 of 2004 pending in the Court of Senior Special Judge, Narayanganj should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Complainant, Hamida Begum, Senior Teacher and Teacher Representative of Narayanganj High School filed a petition of complaint on 24.1.2004 before the Court of Senior Special Judge, Narayanganj being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 253 of 2004 against the accused petitioner alleging that the accused petitioner was appointed as Head Master of Narayanganj High School on 25.7.1992. For his financial mismanagement or the school fund his financial power was withdrawn and given to Mr. Joynal Abedin, Senior Teacher by the managing committee of the School on 6.4.1993. The accused petitioner some months after with the help of some of the members of unapproved managing committee took the financial power. During 1992-1993 he misappropriated Tk.2,20,718./-, in respect of salary of the government part of 3 teachers. He misappropriated Tk.8.00,000/- in the name of development of the school. He took away 4 partitions and 6 tables of segun wood from 1.12.1994 to 15.1.1995. He collected coaching money from the S.S.C. candidates to the tune of Tk.1,57,500/- and without disturbing the same among the teachers misappropriated the same. He misappropriated Tk.1,00,000/- from the salary cut of the teachers in the name of provident fund but did not deposit. He misappropriated Tk.1,00,000/- in the year 2001 by selling namaz ghor of the school. Thus the accused petitioner as Head Master of the School has misappropriated the money fraudently thereby committed breach of trust. 

 3. The petition of complaint was registered as criminal Miscellaneous Case No.253 of 2004. The learned Sessions Judge, Narayanganj sent the petition of complaint to the Magistrate for enquiry and report by the order dated 24.1.2004. The concerned Magistrate submitted his report on 15.2.2004. The learned Sessions Judge again sent the matter to the enquiry officer for further enquiry by the order dated 24.2.2004 and after enquiry report was submitted. Thereafter cognizance was taken under sections 408/409/420 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 against the accused petitioner on 8.3.2004 and registered the case as Special Case No. 2 of 2004. 

 4. The accused petitioner was enlarged on bail by this Court on 29.3.2004 in criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2402 of 2004. Charge was framed against him in his absence on 1.8.2004 under sections 408/409/420 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. In the case 3 witnesses have been examined in Chief in the absence of the accused petitioner on 6.1.2005. 

 5. Thereafter the accused petitioner moved this Court with this application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the proceedings of the case and obtained this Rule. At the time of issuance of the Rule on 24.5.2005 further proceedings of the case was stayed initially for a period of 6 months which subsequently has been extended from time to time. 

 10. Section 4 of the Act provides the jurisdiction of a Special Judge for taking cognizance and trial of the offences committed by the persons stated above. Since we found that the alleged offence committed by the accused petitioner who is neither a Public Servant nor he acted with or abated or attempted to abate or acted in conspiracy with any Public Servant, taking cognizance, framing charge and commencing trial against him by the Special Judge against him for the alleged offence punishable under section 408/409/420 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 is without jurisdiction. In the case though 3 witnesses have been examined in chief for the prosecution yet the proceeding of the case can not be continued against the accused petitioner as being corum nonjudice. 

 11. For the reasons discussed above we are of the view that taking cognizence, framing charge and commencing trial of the case against the accused petitioner for the offence alleged by the learned Special Judge is without jurisdiction and hence continuation of the proceedings of the case will be a sheer abuse of process of the court and hence liable to be quashed. 

 12. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned proceeding of Special Case No. 2 of 2004 pending before the Senior Special Judge, Narayanganj against the accused petitioner is quashed. 

 14. Communicate a copy of this judgment to the Court below where the case is pending.
